description: Every stored result of the Humanities Data Benchmark, as joinable Parquet tables with a metric dictionary. Apart from the framework's own test benchmarks, nothing is filtered: runs that failed, were never scored, or whose configuration is no longer known are rows carrying a status, not omissions.
name: humanities-data-benchmark-results

relatedIdentifiers.note: concept DOI of the software that produced these results

fields.description: Primary key: `<benchmark>.<level>.<source_metric>`.
fields.name: metric_id

fields.description: Which benchmark defines this metric.
fields.name: benchmark

fields.description: `run`, `request` or `field`.
fields.name: level

fields.description: The key as the scorer writes it.
fields.name: source_metric

fields.description: `performance` for a measurement, `count` for a tally, `parameter` for a setting the scorer was given. Averaging across roles is meaningless.
fields.name: metric_role

fields.description: `ratio_0_1`, `error_rate`, `iou`, or a count noun.
fields.name: unit

fields.description: `higher_better`, `lower_better`, or `not_applicable` for counts and parameters.
fields.name: direction

fields.description: Lower bound where the metric has one.
fields.name: min_value

fields.description: Upper bound where the metric has one.
fields.name: max_value

fields.description: How this metric may be combined: `sum` for counts, `mean_over_requests`, `not_summable` for a ratio already averaged by the scorer, `not_aggregatable` for a parameter.
fields.name: aggregation

fields.description: What the metric measures and how it was produced.
fields.name: description

fields.description: Foreign key to `runs.run_id`.
fields.name: run_id

fields.description: The input's identity within its benchmark, taken from the request filename. A string: leading zeros and non-ASCII characters are significant. Null when the filename resolved to no id, which is a release-blocking diagnostic rather than a normal state.
fields.name: object_id

fields.description: Denormalised from `runs`, for filtering without a join.
fields.name: test_id

fields.description: Denormalised from `runs`.
fields.name: date

fields.description: Denormalised from `runs`.
fields.name: benchmark

fields.description: Path of the request file in the source archive.
fields.name: source_path

fields.description: Integer line number, populated only when the whole object id matches `line_<digits>`. Presentation metadata; never a join key.
fields.name: line

fields.description: Provider from the test configuration.
fields.name: configured_provider

fields.description: Model from the test configuration.
fields.name: configured_model

fields.description: Provider as the stored response reports it. This and the configured provider are both exported because they disagree for aliased and routed models; neither is substituted for the other.
fields.name: response_provider

fields.description: Model as the stored response reports it. For routed providers this is what actually served the request.
fields.name: response_model

fields.description: Whether the stored file could be read: `ok`, `missing`, `unreadable`, `invalid`. Describes reading the file, not whether the model's own output parsed.
fields.name: parse_status

fields.description: The timestamp exactly as stored. Naive local time throughout this corpus, with no offset recorded.
fields.name: timestamp_raw

fields.description: UTC conversion, populated only where the source carries an offset. Null for every row in this release, because no stored timestamp does and the writing machine's timezone is not recorded.
fields.name: timestamp_utc

fields.description: Wall-clock seconds the request took, as recorded. Absent on some error records.
fields.name: duration_s

fields.description: Completion reason reported by the provider.
fields.name: finish_reason

fields.description: True when the record carries an explicit error field. Null when it cannot be assessed, for instance when the file did not parse. Not a general success verdict.
fields.name: is_error

fields.description: The recorded error text, where present. Records holding nothing but this and `finish_reason` `error` stand for answers that were billed but dropped unsaved by a runner bug (runs of 2026-09-16 to 2026-10-26); they are scored as misses, and their tokens and cost are unknown.
fields.name: error_message

fields.description: Same vocabulary as `runs.scoring_status`, applied to this request's own stored score.
fields.name: scoring_status

fields.description: Whether this request carries a real scoring observation, by its benchmark's own rule: a performance metric, or the complete set of counts a counting scorer uses. `business_letters` needs all three true-positive categories, since one is a partial observation. A parameter such as `iou_threshold` does not qualify, nor do the fixed placeholders the scaffold benchmarks emit. This is the column `runs.n_scored` counts.
fields.name: is_scored

fields.description: Prompt tokens as recorded. Null when no usage block was stored, which is not the same as zero.
fields.name: input_tokens

fields.description: Completion tokens as recorded.
fields.name: output_tokens

fields.description: Total tokens as recorded. Not necessarily the sum of the two above.
fields.name: total_tokens

fields.description: Cached prompt tokens, where the provider reported them.
fields.name: cached_tokens

fields.description: Cache-write tokens, where reported.
fields.name: cache_creation_tokens

fields.description: Cache-read tokens, where reported.
fields.name: cache_read_tokens

fields.description: Billed reasoning tokens not already counted in `output_tokens`: the provider's own reasoning count, clamped to `total_tokens - input_tokens - output_tokens`, so input + output + reasoning = total. Zero for providers that count reasoning inside output tokens. Null when no total was recorded.
fields.name: reasoning_tokens

fields.description: Input cost as the request file holds it. Never recomputed here.
fields.name: stored_input_cost_usd

fields.description: Output cost as the request file holds it.
fields.name: stored_output_cost_usd

fields.description: Total cost as the request file holds it, reasoning included. Costed at run time against the price table then live, or filled in afterwards at the price in force on the run's date where the run recorded none.
fields.name: stored_estimated_cost_usd

fields.description: Reasoning cost as the request file holds it: reasoning tokens at the output price in force on the run's date. Null where there was no reasoning outside output tokens or no price was in force.
fields.name: stored_reasoning_cost_usd

fields.description: Recomputed here: `input_tokens / 1e6 × the input price in force on the run's date`.
fields.name: derived_input_cost_usd

fields.description: Recomputed here, from output tokens and the output price.
fields.name: derived_output_cost_usd

fields.description: Recomputed here, from `reasoning_tokens` and the output price. Null when reasoning tokens are unknown.
fields.name: derived_reasoning_cost_usd

fields.description: Sum of the derived input, output and reasoning costs, and null unless input and output were both derivable -- see `cost_provenance`. Uniform across the corpus and reproducible from the price table, but it is what the run would have cost at that date's prices, not what was charged.
fields.name: derived_total_cost_usd

fields.description: `derived` when input, output and reasoning tokens were all known and priced. `derived_reasoning_unknown` when no total was recorded, so reasoning is unknown and the total covers input and output only. `partial_tokens` when only one of input and output was: the known component is exported, the total is null, and the missing side is never assumed to be zero. Otherwise why no cost could be derived at all: `no_price_in_table`, `no_tokens`, `no_model_identity`.
fields.name: cost_provenance

fields.description: Which dated entry in the price table was used. Not the run's date: the nearest entry at or before it.
fields.name: pricing_bucket_date

fields.description: How stale that entry was at the run's date. Large values mean the table had a gap, not that the price was wrong.
fields.name: pricing_age_days

fields.description: Input price used for the derived cost.
fields.name: pricing_input_price_per_million

fields.description: Output price used for the derived cost.
fields.name: pricing_output_price_per_million

fields.description: The name matched in the price table, after alias resolution.
fields.name: pricing_model_key

fields.description: `response` when the stored response's own provider/model was priced, `config` when it fell back to the configured pair.
fields.name: pricing_identity_source

fields.description: Provider-side conversation identifier, where recorded.
fields.name: conversation_id

fields.description: Whether the record stored a parsed structured output. The parsed value itself is in the payload sidecar.
fields.name: has_parsed

fields.description: Whether the record stored the raw provider envelope.
fields.name: has_raw_response

fields.description: Foreign key to `runs.run_id`.
fields.name: run_id

fields.description: Foreign key component to `requests`.
fields.name: object_id

fields.description: Which benchmark scored this, from the test configuration.
fields.name: benchmark

fields.description: The field compared, exactly as the scorer keyed it.
fields.name: field_path

fields.description: Per-field similarity as the scorer computes it **today**. Null where the scorer assigns no similarity, as the counting scorers do.
fields.name: score

fields.description: Whether re-scoring this input reproduces the score its run stored. Null when the run stored none to compare against. False means the ground truth or the scorer has changed since -- 12 inputs in this release.
fields.name: reproduces_stored_score

fields.description: When the re-scoring ran. Not when the benchmark ran.
fields.name: rescored_date

fields.description: Commit that last touched the benchmark's scorer at that point.
fields.name: scorer_revision

fields.description: Commit that last touched the benchmark's ground truths.
fields.name: ground_truth_revision

fields.description: Whether the scorer or ground truths had uncommitted changes when the re-scoring ran, which makes the two revisions above incomplete descriptions of the code that produced these numbers.
fields.name: scorer_dirty

fields.description: Primary key: `<test_id>@<date>`. Identifies a stored run directory within this release. A test executed on another date is a different run.
fields.name: run_id

fields.description: The test configuration's id, as the run directory is named. Preserved exactly, including variant spellings that no longer appear in the configuration file.
fields.name: test_id

fields.description: The date folder the run was stored under, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Not a timestamp: it is the directory name, and the runner writes to it for the duration of a run.
fields.name: date

fields.description: Which benchmark this run belongs to, from the test configuration. Null when the test id could not be resolved.
fields.name: benchmark

fields.description: The benchmark version the run was made with: the version in force at its first request (inputs, prompts, schema and scorer as they then were), from the benchmark's version history. Null for a benchmark without one.
fields.name: benchmark_version

fields.description: The version whose scorer and ground truth the stored scores stand under: the latest re-scoring of the benchmark made on or after the run's day, else `benchmark_version`. A re-scoring checks every stored run and labels only those whose scores changed, so unlabelled runs count too. Scores share a basis when the major number is the same; before 1.0.0, when 0.y is.
fields.name: benchmark_version_scored

fields.description: How `benchmark_version` was found. `recorded`: the runner recorded it, with the benchmark's files as committed. `inferred`: from the run's time and when each version was committed. `ambiguous`: recorded while the benchmark's files had uncommitted changes, a run resumed from answers made with another benchmark state, or inferred for a run made earlier on the day a version took effect (or that day at an unknown time); the next version is also possible.
fields.name: benchmark_version_basis

fields.description: Path of the run directory in the source archive, for tracing a row back to the bytes it came from.
fields.name: source_path

fields.description: `matched` when the test id resolves in the configuration file, `unknown_test_id` when it does not. An unknown id keeps its exact spelling and its configuration-derived columns stay null.
fields.name: config_status

fields.description: Provider named in the test configuration. May differ from the provider that actually served the requests -- see `requests.response_provider`.
fields.name: configured_provider

fields.description: Model named in the test configuration. May differ from the model that actually served the requests.
fields.name: configured_model

fields.description: Structured-output class the run requested, if any.
fields.name: dataclass

fields.description: Sampling temperature configured for the run. Null when not configured, which is not the same as zero.
fields.name: temperature

fields.description: System-role text configured for the run.
fields.name: role_description

fields.description: Name of the prompt file used. The prompt's contents are not exported; prompts changed over the corpus and this records only which was named.
fields.name: prompt_file

fields.description: The run's `rules` column verbatim, as a JSON string. Some benchmarks select which fields they score from it, so two runs of one benchmark with different rules are not directly comparable.
fields.name: rules_json

fields.description: True when the configuration marks this test as deprecated.
fields.name: legacy_test

fields.description: The benchmark's `display` metadata flag. True when the metadata loaded and did not set it to false; null when metadata could not be read.
fields.name: benchmark_display

fields.description: The default analytical view excludes these. True when the test is legacy or the benchmark sets `display: false`; false only when both inputs are known and neither hides the run; null when either is unresolved. Filter on `hidden = false` rather than `hidden != true`: null is not a licence to include.
fields.name: hidden

fields.description: Request files discovered in the run directory. The denominator for the coverage fractions below.
fields.name: n_requests

fields.description: Request files that parsed as JSON. Lower than `n_requests` when a stored file is malformed.
fields.name: n_valid_requests

fields.description: Requests whose stored record carries a truthy `error` or `error_message`. Not a general failure count: a request can fail without recording either.
fields.name: n_explicit_errors

fields.description: Requests where `requests.is_scored` is true -- a performance metric, or the complete counts a counting scorer uses. Not the scorer's own `n`, and it does not certify that every expected document was scored: it counts observations that exist, not observations that should.
fields.name: n_scored

fields.description: Whether a `scoring.json` file exists. True even when that file only records that scoring is not implemented.
fields.name: has_scoring

fields.description: One of `missing`, `invalid`, `not_implemented` (the scorer wrote `niy`), `no_numeric_metrics`, `numeric_metrics_present`.
fields.name: scoring_status

fields.description: Copied verbatim from the run's own cost summary.
fields.name: recorded_total_input_tokens

fields.description: Copied verbatim from the run's own cost summary.
fields.name: recorded_total_output_tokens

fields.description: Copied verbatim from the run's own cost summary. Excludes reasoning billed outside output tokens.
fields.name: recorded_total_tokens

fields.description: Copied verbatim from the run's own cost summary. The runner does not write it, so null does not mean zero; sum the request-level `reasoning_tokens` instead.
fields.name: recorded_total_reasoning_tokens

fields.description: Copied verbatim from the run's own cost summary. Null where reasoning was recorded but no price was in force.
fields.name: recorded_reasoning_cost_usd

fields.description: Copied verbatim from the run's own cost summary. Not recomputed, and its completeness is unknown.
fields.name: recorded_input_cost_usd

fields.description: Copied verbatim from the run's own cost summary.
fields.name: recorded_output_cost_usd

fields.description: Copied verbatim from the run's own cost summary. The runner initialises this to zero and skips requests with no cost, so it may already be an understatement.
fields.name: recorded_total_cost_usd

fields.description: Pricing bucket the run costed itself against, where its cost summary records one. Only the longer summary shape carries it.
fields.name: recorded_pricing_date

fields.description: Input price the run costed itself against, where recorded.
fields.name: recorded_input_price_per_million

fields.description: Output price the run costed itself against, where recorded.
fields.name: recorded_output_price_per_million

fields.description: Requests in this run carrying a finite stored total cost, zero included.
fields.name: n_requests_with_stored_cost

fields.description: Sum of those stored costs. An observed subtotal, not an estimate of what the requests without one would have cost.
fields.name: observed_stored_cost_usd

fields.description: `n_requests_with_stored_cost / n_requests`. Null for a run with no requests.
fields.name: stored_cost_coverage_fraction

fields.description: True only when every saved request in this run has a stored cost. Says nothing about attempts that were never saved.
fields.name: stored_cost_complete_for_saved_requests

fields.description: Requests in this run for which a cost could be derived from recorded tokens and the price table.
fields.name: n_requests_with_derived_cost

fields.description: Sum of those derived costs.
fields.name: observed_derived_cost_usd

fields.description: `n_requests_with_derived_cost / n_requests`.
fields.name: derived_cost_coverage_fraction

fields.description: The benchmark's tags, as a JSON string. Describes the benchmark at export time, not necessarily at run time.
fields.name: tags_json

fields.description: The benchmark's contributors, as a JSON string.
fields.name: contributors_json

fields.description: Foreign key to `runs.run_id`.
fields.name: run_id

fields.description: Foreign key component to `requests`. Null for run-level observations.
fields.name: object_id

fields.description: `run`, `request` or `field`.
fields.name: level

fields.description: Which field a field-level observation refers to, preserved exactly as the scorer keyed it -- including the empty string, which is a real key for several thousand observations. Non-null exactly when `level` is `field`; that invariant is how the CSV distinguishes an empty path from a null one.
fields.name: field_path

fields.description: Foreign key to `metrics.metric_id`. Scoped by benchmark and level, because the same metric name means different things in different benchmarks.
fields.name: metric_id

fields.description: The observation. Finite numbers only; a non-numeric score is not represented here at all, and its absence is recorded in `scoring_status` instead.
fields.name: value

fields.description: Which exported table the column belongs to.
fields.name: table

fields.description: The column being measured.
fields.name: column

fields.description: How the rows were grouped: `global`, `benchmark`, `configured_provider`, `date`, or `benchmark+provider+date`.
fields.name: group_dimension

fields.description: The group. `<null>` where the grouping column itself is null -- those rows are retained rather than dropped.
fields.name: group_value

fields.description: Rows in this group. The denominator.
fields.name: n_rows

fields.description: Rows where the column has a value.
fields.name: n_non_null

fields.description: Rows where it does not. Null means not recorded, never an inferred zero.
fields.name: n_null

fields.description: Rows where a numeric column holds a non-finite value. Zero throughout this release: the extractor rejects them, and the count is kept so that a future regression is visible rather than silent.
fields.name: n_invalid

fields.description: `n_non_null / n_rows`.
fields.name: fraction_non_null
